newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire premier to move into his office Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Zaire premier to move into his office Wednesday.

text.p: Zaire's new prime minister, Etienne Tshisekedi, facing stiff political opposition after less than a week in the job, will formally move into his offices on Wednesday, state radio reported.

Leading Zairean politicians had met in parliament on Tuesday after slipping past angry Tshisekedi supporters who were trying to deny them access and prevent them ousting the radical politician from the job.

But one participant said procedural differences prevented agreement on how to oust Tshisekedi, who faces an unlikely alliance of supporters of President Mobutu Sese Seko and alienated former allies of Tshisekedi in the radical opposition.

Witnesses said one lawmaker from the radical opposition was hospitalised after being hit by stones while trying to enter parliament at the front. Another had his trousers ripped off and a third had his car windscreen smashed.
"The Prime Minister Etienne Tshisekedi takes official control of his offices tomorrow. His motorcade leaves his private residence at 9 a.m. (0800 GMT)," the radio said.

Militant Tshisekedi supporters prevented parliament launching its new session on Monday but parliament's vice-president, Andre Boboliko, from the opposition alliance, said the session could be considered open anyway.
Those legislators who met in parliament on Tuesday did so as its organising committees.
"So far no one has put forward a motion of no-confidence," Boboliko said on Tuesday. "In order to do so they have first to collect the signatures of at least 185 deputies."

The deputy leader of Mobutu's Popular Revolutionary Movement (MPR), Banza Mukalayi, told Reuters the parties were committed to dismissing Tshisekedi. "There is hesitation over the procedures that will be used," he said.
The outgoing cabinet of prime minister Kengo wa Dondo is still occupying government buildings, but most official business is halted because of the crisis, officials say.

Tshisekedi, a veteran Mobutu foe, was appointed after parliament voted out Kengo following persistent charges that he mismanaged the government's war against Laurent Kabila's rebels who took up arms in October.
Tshisekedi alienated Mobutu's allies and even his own opposition backers by excluding all but his most loyal followers from a cabinet he announced on his first day in power last week.
The opposition alliance that helped return him to the job from which he was sacked by Mobutu four years ago ganged up with rivals in an attempt to unseat the new prime minister.
But Tshisekedi's fanatical supporters moved in force to pre-empt a parliamentary vote against their hero, battling troops on Monday and frightening off lawmakers.
